facts: Coordinates are written $(x, y)$ — **horizontal first**, then vertical.
$x$ is counted along from $0$; $y$ is counted up from $0$.
The point $(0, 0)$ is the **origin**, where the axes meet.
steps: Move right by the first coordinate ($x$).
Move up by the second coordinate ($y$), then mark the point.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Start at the origin and use the horizontal coordinate first, then the vertical coordinate.

 a. Right $4$, up $3$: $K$.

 b. Right $3$, up $4$: $L$.

 c. Right $2.5$, up $1$: $M$.

 d. Right $1$, up $2.5$: $N$.

For $M$, the horizontal position is halfway between $2$ and $3$. For $N$, the vertical position is halfway between $2$ and $3$.

foundation.solution_text:
Move $2$ units right, then $4$ units up.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]
\draw[gray!30,very thin] (0,0) grid (6,6);\draw[->] (0,0)--(6.5,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,6.5) node[above] {$y$};\fill (2,4) circle (2.5pt) node[above right] {$A$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
$A=(2,4)$

Move $5$ units right, then $1$ unit up.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]
\draw[gray!30,very thin] (0,0) grid (6,6);\draw[->] (0,0)--(6.5,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,6.5) node[above] {$y$};\fill (5,1) circle (2.5pt) node[above right] {$B$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
$B=(5,1)$

Move $3$ units right, then $3$ units up.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]
\draw[gray!30,very thin] (0,0) grid (6,6);\draw[->] (0,0)--(6.5,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,6.5) node[above] {$y$};\fill (3,3) circle (2.5pt) node[above right] {$C$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
$C=(3,3)$

The first coordinate is $0$, so stay on the $y$-axis and move $5$ units up.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]
\draw[gray!30,very thin] (0,0) grid (6,6);\draw[->] (0,0)--(6.5,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,6.5) node[above] {$y$};\fill (0,5) circle (2.5pt) node[above right] {$D$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
$D=(0,5)$

Move $4$ units right. The second coordinate is $0$, so stay on the $x$-axis.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]
\draw[gray!30,very thin] (0,0) grid (6,6);\draw[->] (0,0)--(6.5,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,6.5) node[above] {$y$};\fill (4,0) circle (2.5pt) node[above right] {$E$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
$E=(4,0)$

Both coordinates are $0$, so the point is where the axes meet.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.75]
\draw[gray!30,very thin] (0,0) grid (6,6);\draw[->] (0,0)--(6.5,0) node[right] {$x$};\draw[->] (0,0)--(0,6.5) node[above] {$y$};\fill (0,0) circle (2.5pt) node[above right] {$O$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
$O=(0,0)$
